_comment: IMPL #168 recall battery fixture (COMMITTED, never generated at runtime). Ground-truth is calibrated to the pipeline: MemChorus recall is lexical exact-term-match + half-life recency (NOT semantic), so each query's 'expected_keys' are the two records that genuinely share 3-4 unigrams with the query, and pair members are age-close (<= ~4d apart) so recall measures topical matching, not recency. Content uses <profile>-style placeholders; no real usernames, paths, machines, or tokens (OPSEC). Corpus: 26 signal records (12 clean topical pairs + 2 near-identical + 2 unpaired realistic candidates), 1 byte-identical dedup pair, 40 noise records, and a self-contained source-scoping probe (searched in its own isolated dirs, not this corpus).

signal.text: canary deploy runbook: stage the rollout on the staging cluster first, watch error budgets, then promote to production in waves.
lessons from the last canary deploy: promote gradually, keep the rollback path warm, and alert on p99 latency regressions during the rollout.
the database migration script failed on the orders table: verify constraints and run the migration in a transaction with a clean rollback path.
database migration runbook: snapshot the schema, apply in a maintenance window, verify row counts against the previous table before dropping columns.
pytest coverage gate: keep the suite green, hold coverage above the threshold, and re-run the full matrix before pushing changes.
qa verification checklist: run pytest until the suite is green, confirm the coverage gate passed, then push the changes to the remote branch.
code review policy: require two approvals, run the CI checks, and merge only after the quality gate passes and feedback is resolved.
review checklist before you merge: verify types, verify tests, and make sure CI is green across the whole matrix.
sync jobs: the nightly batch should checkpoint per shard so a restart resumes cleanly instead of replaying every record twice.
nightly batch: shard the ingestion window and checkpoint progress per shard so a mid-run failure resumes without duplicate work.
memory hygiene: keep the memory file compact, prune stale notes, and keep every line high-signal so context stays useful.
context management: compress conversation history, keep the working context tight, and prune dead ends from the scratch notes.
release process: cut a tagged release from the main branch, verify checksums, and publish the signed artifacts to the registry.
release artifacts: verify the checksums, publish signed artifacts to the registry, and tag the release from the main branch.
alerting policy: tune the observability alert threshold before the rollout so noisy pings do not mask real incidents.
observability tuning: set the alert threshold, route paging correctly, and keep the rollout dashboard fresh.
dependency policy: pin exact versions in the lockfile, avoid drift between environments, and audit third-party packages before upgrading.
lockfile hygiene: pin exact versions in the lockfile, avoid drift between environments, and audit upgrades before merging.
api compatibility: keep the response schema stable for existing integrations, or document a deprecation window before you change fields.
api stability: hold the response schema stable for existing integrations and document a deprecation window before changing fields.
error recovery: read the full traceback top to bottom, reproduce the failure deterministically, and fix the root cause rather than silencing it.
failure triage: read the full traceback, reproduce the error deterministically, and fix the root cause not the symptom.
versioning notes: bump the patch level after each release, align the changelog, and keep the runtime version in sync with package metadata.
changelog discipline: align the changelog, bump the patch level after each release, and keep the runtime version in sync with package metadata.
tooling notes: keep the sandbox venv pinned, avoid global pip upgrades mid-task, and document the exact tool versions used.
session librarian: keep the scratch notes tidy, prune dead ends from the working context, and preserve the useful high-signal lines.

dedup_pair._comment: Two keys with BYTE-IDENTICAL text. Content-level dedup must collapse them to at most one in every top-k set. A query ('identical dedup pair') targets only these two.
dedup_pair.text: identical dedup pair: this exact sentence is stored verbatim under two different keys to probe content-level dedup in the recall pipeline.
